trial_court: Family Court, Bokaro, Original Suit No. 262 of 2016
case_name: Bhola Lal Srivastav vs Khushi Devi
facts_of_case: The parties were married in 2008 and had two children. The wife left the husband's house in 2013 without giving any information. The husband made attempts to reconcile but was refused. A suit for divorce was filed by the husband.

legal_principles.principle: A direction to pay permanent alimony without there being any discussion, appreciation, reasoning and categorical findings on the material issues is wholly unsustainable in law.
legal_principles.held: In our view, mere perusal of the order of the Family Court and the High Court quoted supra, would go to show that both the Courts failed to apply their judicial mind to the factual and legal controversy insofar as award of permanent alimony to the respondent (wife) is concerned.

legal_principles.principle: Courts must apply their judicial mind to the factual and legal controversy before awarding permanent alimony.
legal_principles.held: Both the Courts did not even mention the factual narration of the case set up by the parties on the question of award of permanent alimony and without there being any discussion, appreciation, reasoning and categorical findings on the material issues such as, financial earning capacity of husband to pay the alimony and also the financial earning capacity of wife, a direction to pay Rs.15,00,000/- by way of permanent alimony to the wife was given.

outcome.final_order: The appellant has been directed to make payment of Rs. 5,00,000/- as permanent alimony to the respondent.

keywords: Latin maxim: Nemo dat quod non habet
